conflicts.point: Whether generative AI adoption results in net workforce augmentation or net job displacement and increased error-correction burdens.

positions.stance: Deploying generative AI eliminates redundant tasks and shifts human labor to higher-value problem solving, resulting in broader economic augmentation.
Enterprise deployments cut support roles and transfer unverified output onto remaining staff, increasing error-correction burdens and operational risk.

conflicts.point: Whether labor boards and unions should use statutory mechanisms like Section 8(a)(5) of the National Labor Relations Act to govern automated task redesign.

positions.stance: Regulatory oversight and collective bargaining mandates create harmful bottlenecks that delay innovation and critical societal progress.
Existing labor board authorities must govern task-redesign pathways to protect workers from sudden displacement and uncompensated verification labor.

verdicts.conflict: Whether generative AI adoption results in net workforce augmentation or net job displacement and increased error-correction burdens.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position prevails on empirical evidence because it documents measurable drops in administrative support roles following enterprise deployments. The accelerationist claim relies on generalized assertions about higher-value problem solving without comparable workforce metrics.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Robust longitudinal employment data showing that firms adopting generative AI experience net job growth and verifiable transitions of displaced staff into higher-value roles would shift the balance.

verdicts.conflict: Whether labor boards and unions should use statutory mechanisms like Section 8(a)(5) of the National Labor Relations Act to govern automated task redesign.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position provides concrete implementation specificity by identifying existing statutory mechanisms under the National Labor Relations Act to govern task redesign. The accelerationist position relies on abstract warnings about innovation bottlenecks without detailing alternative enforcement frameworks.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical evidence demonstrating that labor board oversight systematically halts productivity growth across entire economic sectors would validate the accelerationist concern over regulatory bottlenecks.
